figures.finding: Iraq's Civil Code (No. 40 of 1951) sets majority at eighteen full years, as the Government reported to the UN; the age of discretion is seven.
figures.applies: Iraq; Civil Code arts. 106 and 97(2), as the State reports them (the code's own text not read).

sources.said: article 106 thereof states that the age of majority is 18 full years and article 97, paragraph 2, states that the age of discretion is 7 full years.

figures.finding: The minimum age for admission to work in Iraq is fifteen; "juveniles" are those under eighteen, as the Government reported of the Labour Act No. 71 of 1987 (since replaced by the Labour Law No. 37 of 2015, not read); the Kurdistan Region likewise bars employment under fifteen.
figures.applies: Iraq; the State's report of 2013 on the 1987 Act; the 2015 Labour Law's own text not read.

sources.said: The minimum age for admission to a job or work within Iraqi territory and to means of transport registered in Iraqi territory shall be 15 years;

sources.title: Iraq: combined second to fourth periodic reports to the Committee on the Rights of the Child, CRC/C/IRQ/2-4 (2013, issued 7 March 2014); quotes the Iraqi Civil Code No. 40 of 1951, arts. 97 and 106
sources.said: article 106 thereof states that the age of majority is 18 full years and article 97, paragraph 2, states that the age of discretion is 7 full years. … The minimum age for admission to a job or work within Iraqi territory and to means of transport registered in Iraqi territory shall be 15 years;
